join_order.notes: Single literal scan over keyword.keyword to resolve target_k_id; then CSR slice yields candidate mk rows (small).
title is dense PK; production_year_bin[t_id-1] > 2014 && != INT32_MIN (selectivity ~5% of candidates).

join_order.probe: cast_info.person_id within offsets_only slice per surviving t_id
join_order.notes: Very selective LIKE produces a tiny set; small hash_set used for IN-test inside ci slice.

data_structures.aggregation: three scalar MIN trackers (k.keyword is constant literal; n.name and t.title compared as std::string_view)

parallelism.notes: mk slice for one keyword id is tiny (~few hundred rows); parallel overhead would exceed work. name pre-scan can optionally be parallel over 12 threads since it scans 4.17M varlen rows.

execution_notes: MIN(k.keyword) resolves to the literal 'marvel-cinematic-universe' if any row matches; track presence via a boolean rather than re-reading.
Pre-scan name.name in parallel (12 threads) using offsets+dat; per-row check substring 'Downey' then 'Robert' after it. Append matching n.id to thread-local vectors then merge into flat_hash_set.
Pre-scan keyword.keyword sequentially (only 134K rows, varlen) to find target_k_id; if not found, return three NULLs.

Main loop: lo=mk_off[target_k_id], hi=mk_off[target_k_id+1]; for j in [lo,hi): mk_row=mk_rowids[j]; t_id=mk_movie_id[mk_row]; if production_year_bin[t_id-1] > 2014 && != INT32_MIN: walk ci_off[t_id]..ci_off[t_id+1]; if downey_robert_ids.contains(ci_person[r]) update MIN(n.name) and MIN(t.title) lazily (only fetch varlen on first match per t_id/person_id).
Use std::string_view comparisons against current best to avoid copying; only copy on update.
